subject.title: fix(agents): subagent model precedence — global default shadowed by parent agent's own model

question: Should `agents.defaults.subagents.model` outrank an agent's own primary model in `resolveSubagentModelConfigSelectionResult` and isolated cron subagent selection?
rationale: Docs and the direct native resolver now support global subagent default precedence, but the shared helper and cron tests still encode the opposite compatibility-sensitive behavior.

options.title: Accept documented precedence
options.body: Land the focused linked PR or an equivalent helper/cron change so per-agent subagent config wins first, global subagent default wins second, and agent primary is last-resort fallback.

options.title: Keep agent-primary precedence
options.body: Close the linked fix path and update public subagent docs plus tests to describe that an agent primary intentionally shadows the global subagent default in these paths.

options.title: Sequence with runtime persistence
options.body: Decide this rule together with https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/72984 so spawn planning, cron, session persistence, and runtime launch do not diverge.

recommendation.title: Accept documented precedence
recommendation.body: Land the focused linked PR or an equivalent helper/cron change so per-agent subagent config wins first, global subagent default wins second, and agent primary is last-resort fallback.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is the strongest available decision-route signal from prior maintainer-facing review and current adjacent file history.
